hypotheses.justification: The definition of smoothedFundamental uses finsum and requires no finite-index instance. Set f δ := puCut T (mob δ τ); hasFiniteSupport_puCut_mob proves its support finite for every T and τ. Pull this support back along cosetEquiv Γ : (SL(2, ℤ) ⧸ Γ) × Γ ≃ SL(2, ℤ), then take its finite image under Prod.snd. The claimed support is contained in this image: using coe_smul and mob_mob, its value at γ is ∑ᶠ q, f (q.out * γ); if nonzero, some summand is nonzero, since otherwise finsum_eq_zero_of_forall_eq_zero applies. This proof works for arbitrary subgroups, infinite quotients, and empty supports.
